subject.title: feat: heading-aware chunking + entity extraction for memory search

question: Should memory-core change its default chunking semantics to split at markdown headings, add an opt-in chunking strategy, or keep fixed token/overlap chunking until the broader memory MVP direction is settled?
rationale: The source change is tractable, but it changes embedding chunk identity and recall semantics for existing memory indexes, and the issue also bundles broader entity-extraction work.

options.title: Add heading-aware chunking with index identity handling
options.body: Implement the section boundary behavior in memory-core, update index identity/reindex behavior, and keep entity extraction separate.

options.title: Add an opt-in strategy first
options.body: Expose a chunking strategy/config path so existing users retain token-only indexing until they choose a reindex.

options.title: Defer to memory MVP design
options.body: Leave this issue open as product direction until the memory MVP and entity extraction roadmap decides the canonical chunking model.

recommendation.title: Add heading-aware chunking with index identity handling
recommendation.body: Implement the section boundary behavior in memory-core, update index identity/reindex behavior, and keep entity extraction separate.

likelyOwner.reason: Most of the relevant memory-host and memory-plugin history routes through Peter Steinberger, including the refactors that established the current owner boundary.
